title: Basic Calculator II
statement: Evaluate an expression string containing non-negative integers, the operators +, -, *, /, and spaces. Division truncates toward zero. Operator precedence applies: * and / bind tighter than + and -.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: You can delay + and - by pushing signed numbers, and apply * and / immediately to the stack top.
Keep the previous operator. When a number ends, apply that operator.
A trailing sentinel operator forces the last number to be applied.

approaches.name: One stack and last operator
approaches.explanation: Enough when the only precedence split is times/divide versus plus/minus.

editorial: Scan the string and accumulate the current number. When an operator is seen, the previous operator decides what to do with that number. Plus pushes the number, minus pushes its negation, and times or divide combine it with the stack top using truncation toward zero. The answer is the sum of the stack. Processing a final '+' after the loop flushes the last number.
